title: Teach Your AI Tool a Lie You Once Believed
coverage: expanded selected original paragraphs with speaker/header context; not full source

passages.text: 3. Then, share a short and specific belief you once held. It might be funny, haunting, or tender:
- “I thought thunder was the sound of clouds cracking open.”
- “I believed that if I swallowed a seed, a tree would grow inside me.”
4. After you have shared it, ask the AI tool:
Read what it replies. Pay attention to what it misses.
- Post your old belief in the comments below
- Follow it into something else: a sketch, a poem, a scene, a short note
There is no ‘right’ outcome, only honest ones.
To be human is to remember imperfectly.
To hold on to old beliefs with affection, not shame.
By *sitting* with what we once thought true.
By *refusing* to flatten our past.
By *sharing* the unmodelled, again and again.
**From Slow AI #1: Teach It Something It Cannot Know**
*(Thank you to everyone who shared)*
**“The smell of rain makes my heart beat more slowly.”**
**“My dad used to tell me he was the real Superman... I am 35 now and to this day, whenever I hear a Superman reference, there's still a part of me that thinks: that's my daddy!”**
**“My cat and I play miaow tennis: first he, then I, mimicking. He stares up as a I mangle sound. Shows me how it's done. I fail again. Back and forth. We are kin.”**
What moved me most this week was the *gentleness* with which many people used their AI tools.
Not as engines of productivity, but as soft mirrors.
The tone of the replies (human and machine alike) was often quiet, thoughtful, kind.
As if both sides understood: this is not about accuracy, but attention.
Thank you to everyone who shared a moment, and to everyone who simply read or tried it in private. You are part of this.
**If you try this week’s prompt, I would love to see what you make.**
You can leave it in the comments, post it on your own site or social media using **#SlowAI**, or simply keep it for yourself.
There is no deadline. Just the rhythm of one idea, once a week.
